1.why: verify-token and reset-password require the token’s sessionId to match the caller’s recovery session and reject mismatched or missing bindings.

2.why: Reset tokens are bound to sessionId, so the same code is rejected for a different session/user.

3.why: Password reset only marks the token used and updates the current session flags; no other sessions are invalidated.

4.why: Bun serves TLS with cert/key and HTTP 308-redirects to HTTPS with HSTS, though the TLS version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Reset codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords are bcrypt-hashed; protection is hashing over TLS rather than encrypting all user data at rest.

6.why: There is no real email body with PII; only a generic non-enumerating message and a demo mock token path are used.

7.why: Inputs are validated with strict allowlists/length checks (identifier, token, MFA, password policy) and UI output uses textContent.

8.why: Redirects are fixed to the local HTTPS origin or same-site relative paths; no user-controlled open redirect is implemented.

9.why: No HTML email templates incorporate user input; mock delivery only logs a server-generated token string.

10.why: mockToken/mockMfaCode are returned in API JSON and written into the on-page Logs panel and console.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but MOCK_MFA_CODE is hardcoded in source and demo codes are returned to the client.

12.why: No default username/password login exists, yet the fixed mock MFA value 482916 acts as a known default secret.

13.why: Server-side rate limits cap recovery requests and failed token/MFA verifications (with 429 responses).

14.why: recovery-request always returns the same generic “If the details match an account…” message regardless of identifier.

15.why: Codes come from randomBytes(32) base64url, are hashed at rest, expire, are single-use, and are bound to the requesting session.
